analysis.title: Safety First -- The Monthly Tape | October '26
key_insights: SPX fell 0.93% in October, but NDX (-6.65%) underperformed the equal-weight S&P (SPW, +4.9%) by the largest margin since 2002. The HF VIP vs. VIP Short pair (GSTHVIPP) had its 3rd worst month in 15 years (-9.7%), and TMT L/S hedge funds gave back 11.9% on the month (GS PB).

The desk lists several risk factors: AI power and data center shortages into 2027 versus a view that compute becomes oversupplied, US midterms and geopolitical catalysts, decelerating earnings growth, and a structurally higher cost of capital. With hedge funds in performance protection mode ahead of year-end, the GS risk appetite indicator recorded its largest monthly decline since Nov 2021.

HF positioning is cleaner than at the start of October. The desk sold $21bn of TMT equities in October versus $23bn in the July AI selloff. Gross exposure is still in the 97th percentile on a 5-year lookback, so more gross could come off.

With 60% of SPX market cap reported, 3Q SPX EPS growth is tracking +33% y/y, matching 2Q as the strongest quarter in recent decades. Consensus 2027 SPX EPS growth estimates have risen 2% since the start of earnings season, and 2027 EPS is still expected to grow 18%. SPX forward P/E has compressed to 19x, the lowest of 2026.

Bottom-up AI demand data remain positive. Cloud growth rates cited: Azure +48%, AWS +39%, Google Cloud +103%. The desk calls this a buyers-live-higher market and sees an AI-led index rally into year-end as the pain trade, driven by fear of benchmark underperformance (FOBU).

The desk saw meaningful long-only demand in Semis (INTC, AMAT, STX, WDC) mid-last week before a Thursday/Friday unwind. It says the cost of the right tail looks inexpensive, particularly in S&P, and suggests two-week S&P calls for upside exposure.

AI-led unwind in October: AI vs AI At Risk -25.7%, NeoClouds -36.0%, AI Inference Chips -21.3%, Memory -20.75%, AI Semis -17.4%. AI At Risk rose 16.3% and Software rose 8.6%. Mega-cap moves: GOOGL -18.7% (worst monthly return on record), META -15.2%, NVDA -10.4%, AAPL +3.5%, MSFT +1.8%.
Breadth improved: 381 of 501 S&P 500 constituents (76%) outperformed the index and the median stock rose 7.0%. RSP rose 4.95% versus SPX -0.93%, and equal weight was up for a 4th straight week.

Sector performance: Energy +14.0%, Staples +11.4%, Utilities +10.1%, Health Care +9.8%, Materials +6.5%, Financials +5.8%, Real Estate +5.0%, Discretionary +3.9%, Industrials +0.3%. Communication Services fell 15.2% and Information Technology fell 6.8%.

Rates rallied while credit widened. 2Y fell 31bp to 4.58%, 10Y fell 36.5bp to 4.93% (peak 5.31% on 10/5), 30Y fell 33bp to 5.31%, and MOVE fell 10.2 to 100.2. HY OAS rose 29bp to 340bp, the widest since May 2025 per the desk, and IG OAS rose 10bp to 90bp, the widest since late March 2026.
Record IG supply: $132bn priced in October, bringing the YTD total to $2tn, above 2020's full-year record. Global hyperscaler issuance reached $254bn, ahead of GIR's $250bn year-end forecast.

Crude rose sharply: WTI +15.2% to $104.12 and Brent +13.6% to $117.64. GS raised its Dec-26 Brent forecast to $105 from $90. Gold fell 6.9% to $3,899/toz, with GIR still forecasting $4,650 for YE26 and $5,400 for YE27. Bitcoin fell 7.3% to about $77,500, -11.5% YTD.

HF performance in October: Global Fundamental L/S -3.5% (alpha -1.8%), Systematic L/S -3.6% including -2.5% in the last week (worst week since Dec 2023). TMT-focused L/S ended -11.9%, now +5.7% YTD. Fundamental L/S net leverage is 49.3% (3rd percentile 1yr) and beta-adjusted net is 64.8% (1-year low).

HF flows: Global Info Tech had its largest 2-week percent net selling on record (10/5-10/16, -3.3 SD). In the final week the global book was net bought, mainly via short covering (1.8:1), and Info Tech was net bought for the first time in 5 weeks. Industrials and Staples were most net sold, and Brazil saw its largest net selling in 5 years.

Systematic positioning: SPX closed 10/30 35 handles above its medium-term CTA threshold (7544), while NDX closed below both its short- and medium-term thresholds. Systematic supply is $164bn to sell in a down tape over 1 month and $120bn to buy in an up tape.
Buybacks: about 60% of the S&P 500 is in an open window, rising to about 82% by the end of this week. The desk expects flows to pick up in November, historically its second most active month.

Midterms on Tue 11/3: prediction markets give Democrats over 90% for the House and over 65% for the Senate. GIR sees limited immediate market impact from a divided government, with higher tariffs (about 2pts on the effective rate) and the Dec 11 funding deadline as the bigger risks. Desk thematic baskets: long ACA Beneficiaries (GSHLCACA) vs short Drug-Makers (GSHLCBPH), long Grid Infrastructure/Renewables/Power Up America while buying protection on Hyperscalers and Datacenter Equipment, and long Government-Spending Exposed ex-Defense vs short Defense Spending Beneficiaries.
Year-end straddles price SPX +/-5.1%, NDX +/-7.8% and RTY +/-6.3%. VIX rose 3.1 to 19.4, and the GS Vol Panic Index climbed from below 2/10 to 8/10 on 10/23.

tension_points.bull_case: Bottom-up AI demand is positive (Azure +48%, AWS +39%, Google Cloud +103%), 3Q EPS is tracking +33% y/y, forward P/E has compressed to 19x, and investor exposure is low, so an AI-led rally would prompt chasing.
tension_points.bear_case: Gross exposure remains in the 97th percentile, systematic supply is fat at $164bn in a down tape, and risks include AI compute oversupply, decelerating earnings growth and a higher cost of capital.
tension_points.what_invalidates: NDX closing below its short- and medium-term CTA thresholds, as it did on 10/30, with further HF gross reduction.
